subject: Remit-to alias mapping + invoice routing preference (email vs portal)

Subject: Remit alias and invoice delivery - what do you need from us?

Hi Rishi / Kimberly,

We're getting the last bit of set-up in AP before we start receiving monthly invoices. Two quick questions so our ERP mapping is correct: 

1) Remit-to alias: Our payment system uses remit aliases (e.g. ACME-US-AP, ACME-EU-VAT). Can you confirm whether your invoices include a separate Remit-To field the way we need, or do you rely on the envelope From/To header? We can send an example CSV of aliases (attached) — would that help?

2) Delivery channel: Does Redwood push invoices to a webhook/portal by default (with an option to also send an email copy), or do you primarily deliver via email to finance+remit@acmecorp.com? If you support portal webhooks, what fields do you include so we can route by alias?

Also we have one EU entity that requires VAT breakdown per line item — please confirm whether invoices include VAT detail and a VAT ID field.

Thanks,
Sophie Chen
Senior AP Manager, Acme Corp
Attachments: acme_remit_alias_request.csv (csv)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-18T16:22:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Remit alias and invoice delivery - what do you need from us?

Hi Sophie — great questions, thanks for sending the sample. TL;DR: we can support portal-first with an email copy fallback; we also include a discrete "remit_to_alias" field in our invoice payload so you can map in the ERP.

Details: 
- Default flow: if you enroll the account in our Billing Portal (link: https://redwood.app/portal/enroll/ACME-123) invoices are pushed to your configured webhook as JSON. The webhook contains an explicit remit_to_alias field, remit_address, invoice_number, VAT_id (if provided), and line-level VAT amounts.
- Email fallback: if you prefer not to enroll, we can send invoice PDFs to finance+remit@acmecorp.com. The PDF includes the remit-to alias in a top-line field and the VAT breakdown. Note: email PDFs are suitable for human processing but harder to auto-map than the webhook JSON.
- From header vs remit field: we will not rely on the SMTP From header to encode remit routing. We populate the separate remit_to_alias field (and the PDF also shows it). Please consume remit_to_alias for automated routing.

Attachments: I uploaded a CSV with the alias mapping we propose (acme_remit_aliases.csv) based on your sample — please review. Also attaching our standard billing consent template (billing-consent-template.pdf) — we need a signed copy for portal enrollment and to enable webhook delivery.

If you confirm portal enrollment, we can schedule a short webhook test (10–15 minutes) to validate field mapping.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: acme_remit_aliases.csv (csv), billing-consent-template.pdf (pdf)

Hi Sophie — adding a few operational details so your AP team has everything they need: 

1) Signed consent: for webhook delivery we require an onboarding form with an authorized billing contact signature (we accept electronic signatures). The consent also authorizes the portal webhook destination and confirms remit alias mappings.

2) Invoice headers & continuity: the webhook JSON will include the following explicit fields you can rely on for routing: remit_to_alias, remit_to_email, remit_to_address, billing_entity_id (internal), vat_id, invoice_date, due_date, line_items[].line_vat_amount. The PDF will mirror those fields and include a human-readable remit-to block.

3) Change control: if you later ask us to change the remit_to_alias associated with an entity, please raise a formal request via the portal so we can audit the change and provide a signed confirmation for your records.

Marissa — can you confirm whether our billing consent template needs legal redlines for Acme (we usually accept the standard signature page, but we'll accommodate minor edits)?

Kimberly Park
Billing Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
